messages:
ana: Spawning a dedicated thread to capture the cutover playbook for Scoped API Keys (follow-up to the RFC). I want a checklist we can run with staging + Dedicated customers.

ana: Goals: minimize customer impact, provide clear rollback, ensure auditability, and keep high-QPS infra unaffected.

ryan: Quick note: scoped keys are functionally a superset of current API keys. We need clear semantics for operator tokens (long-lived) vs svc projections (short-lived).

meera: Proposal for cutover phases:
1) Inventory + owners: run discovery, produce top-1k tokens by volume with inferred scope + contact. Ship CSV to teams as FYI.
2) Observe-only in staging: enable resolution logging but do not block. Add header X-Auth-Resolution: <resolved> to responses in staging for debugging.
3) Shadow enforcement in prod: validate rules and log rejections but return success. Emit metric auth.scope.shadow_rejects{route}.
4) Soft-enforce per-org: return 403 with a clear error_code and allow an "override" header X-Auth-Override for 5m grace when teams are onboarding.
5) Hard-enforce opt-in: default off. Customer support will coordinate per-org cutovers.

ana: For operator tokens we keep long TTL but require an org tag in inventory. No operator token can be unscoped.

ryan: Runtime details: where do we resolve? At edge (ingress proxy) or application layer? Ingress gives uniformity but needs low-latency cache. App-layer is flexible but inconsistent.

meera: Recommend hybrid: initial resolution at ingress to pick routing/quotas; app layer can re-resolve for fine-grain policy checks. Ingress resolution must be idempotent and cacheable.

vincent: Cache design: local L1 = 2s TTL; shared L2 = 45s; rotation invalidates via webhook. Also include a tombstone when key revoked to avoid stale positives.

ops-bot: schedule: cutover-scan-job queued -> run at 2025-06-03T03:00Z; report will be at https://go/redwood/reports/scoped-keys-discovery-run-1767002222

ana: Error codes and UX:
- 403.scope_mismatch: body contains {"expected":"org-123","resolved":"org-456","how":"inferred"}
- 429.projection_quota: when broker denies ephemeral minting
- 401.malformed: old tokens that don't map to inventory (should route to migration help page)
Make sure Console surfaces the exact error_code and suggested remediation link.

ryan: Third-party integrators: for webhooks and SDK usage we need a migration header response that both documents and advertises steps to rotate: `X-Auth-Migrate: https://go/redwood/migrate-keys`

meera: Rollback criteria: if soft-enforce causes >1% error-rate increase across all requests for 1h, auto-suspend soft-enforce and open incident to eng-sre. Provide a rollback toggle in Console (org-scoped).

vincent: Quirks: some infra tokens have multi-project affinity. We'll support a shared flag and a bounded list of allowed projects. Migration tool will offer to add shared:true during transition.

ana: Broker behavior: ephemeral token payload must include:
- parent_token_id
- audience(s)
- issued_at, expires_at
- projection_hint (svc->svc or job->svc)
Proofs signed by rotating key. Broker must export mint history CSV for audits.

ops-bot: infra-staging branch created: scoped-keys/broker + ingress-hooks. Deploy ETA 2d.

meera: Security punt: what about replay if someone captures ephemeral token? We rely on short TTL + audience claim + per-route nonce for high-value endpoints. Consider mTLS for cross-datacenter service calls.

ryan: Also add anomaly detection: sudden surge in projection requests from a token should alert. We'll tie into existing detection rules.

vincent: Implementation owners: ana -> cutover coordination & CSV; meera -> ingress/shadow enforcement; ryan -> migration scripts & SDK docs; jeff (cc) -> telemetry dashboard (jeff please ack); ops-bot -> runbooks and staging deploy.

ana: final asks before I file the playbook PR: agree timeline and rollback thresholds?

meera: ack timeline and rollback.

ryan: ack.

vincent: ack.

ops-bot: Note: recorded plan saved to https://go/redwood/playbooks/scoped-key-cutover-1767002222
